source_name: Računalniške novice – ICT/fintech trade portal
why_relevant: Slovenian ICT trade press that reprints vendor and fintech press releases nearly verbatim (e.g. GoCrypto 1,000-location milestone), making it a low-friction proxy for local press-release flow that never reaches national dailies.

source_name: Blockchain Alliance Europe (blockchainalliance.si) – membership directory and publications
why_relevant: Ljubljana-based industry association whose member list is effectively a curated roster of Slovenian blockchain/crypto-payments companies — a strong snowballing pointer for actors outside the well-known trio, plus policy-position content.

source_name: SBCA – Slovenian Blockchain Association
why_relevant: Second Slovenian blockchain industry body; complements Blockchain Alliance Europe for actor discovery and for identifying who speaks for the crypto-payments segment in consultations.

source_name: Leanpay – help centre 'Novice' and corporate blog (BNPL)
why_relevant: Slovenia's dominant instalment/BNPL provider (consumer-credit licence from the Ministry of Economy, Tourism and Sport, not Banka Slovenije). Its own news/knowledge pages carry licence, partner-merchant and product changes — the main disclosure channel for the BNPL segment.

source_name: Forbes Slovenija (forbes.n1info.si) – digitalizacija/fintech coverage
why_relevant: Carries company-strategy interviews with Slovenian fintechs (Leanpay) that surface merchant-network scale and growth claims not published elsewhere; useful qualitative complement to registers and filings.

source_name: Mladipodjetnik.si – entrepreneurship portal, fintech/blockchain news
why_relevant: Covers Slovenian participation in EU blockchain initiatives and early-stage fintech activity in Slovenian; low-cost early-signal source for new entrants and policy programmes.

source_name: Bitcoin Društvo Slovenije (bitcoin.si)
why_relevant: Community association maintaining Slovenian-language crypto resources and, historically, merchant-acceptance listings; useful for local terminology and for finding merchants/venues accepting crypto that never issue press releases.

source_name: SloveniaBusiness.eu (SPIRIT Slovenia investment-promotion portal)
why_relevant: Government-backed English-language channel that publicises Slovenian fintech/crypto corporate events (e.g. the Robinhood acquisition of Bitstamp). Reliable English-language pointer to M&A and investment events in this cell.

source_name: HRC d.o.o. — Aktualno (news & case studies, Hibis core banking)
why_relevant: HRC is one of the largest core-banking software suppliers to Slovenian and Croatian banks/savings banks (own Hibis core banking platform). Its news/case-study feed names which bank migrated to which system and when — e.g. Delezna/Deželna banka Slovenije migration to Hibis, OTP banka's merged platform on Hibis, Hibis implementation at Nova KBM, Croatian euro transition. For private Slovenian banks with no procurement trail, this is effectively the public record of core-system selection.

source_name: HRC d.o.o. — O nas (reference customer list)
why_relevant: Explicit named customer roster of Slovenian financial institutions: Addiko Bank, BKS Bank AG, Delavska hranilnica, LON, Primorska hranilnica Vipava, RCI Banque, NLB, Gorenjska banka, Deželna banka Slovenije, OTP banka, Slovenski državni holding. Directly maps vendor-to-bank relationships that never appear in procurement records.

source_name: HRC — Hibis platform product pages
why_relevant: Module-level description of the Hibis core banking platform (what a Slovenian bank actually buys: deposits, loans, payments, mobile/web bank). Useful to interpret which functional layers a bank has outsourced to HRC vs kept elsewhere.

source_name: Halcom d.d. — corporate site (Slovenian)
why_relevant: Halcom is the dominant Slovenian e-banking/digital-signature vendor (Hal E-Bank, Halcom One, qualified certificates). Its own pages state footprint metrics (2 central banks/clearing houses, 50+ commercial banks, 250k+ corporate users, ~13m payments/month, 7 markets) and occasionally announce bank deployments. Primary pointer to which Slovenian banks resell Hal E-Bank.

source_name: Halcom Support / Podpora knowledge base (Hal E-Bank manuals per bank)
why_relevant: Bank-specific Hal E-Bank manuals, version notes and per-market FAQ pages indirectly reveal which banks are live on which Halcom product version and in which country market — a proxy for deployment footprint and upgrade cycles that the marketing site does not disclose.

source_name: Halcom One (digital banking platform site)
why_relevant: Halcom's newer platform brand; separate domain suggests a distinct product/go-to-market line worth tracking for bank onboarding announcements.

source_name: Halcom bank terms & conditions PDFs (Splošni pogoji Hal E-Bank)
why_relevant: Dated, versioned contractual documents in the vendor's uploads directory. They carry effective dates and market scope, and the uploads path (/app/uploads/YYYY/MM/) is itself a harvestable timeline of vendor document releases per market.

source_name: Bank-hosted Hal E-Bank manuals (e.g. UniCredit Bank Slovenija)
why_relevant: A bank publishing a Halcom-branded manual on its own domain is hard confirmation that the bank runs that vendor's product. Searching bank domains for vendor product names is a reliable technique for confirming vendor-bank pairings without any procurement record.

source_name: Mikrografija d.o.o. — References page (mDocs, mSign)
why_relevant: Named financial-sector reference: Delavska hranilnica d.d. using mDocs and mSign (document management / e-signature) with a named contact testimonial. Confirms a document/e-signature vendor inside a Slovenian bank. Testimonials only, no deep case studies.

source_name: Comtrade System Integration — Banking & Finances vertical page
why_relevant: Comtrade SI (Ljubljana office, part of Comtrade Group) publishes banking-vertical customer stories; search results indicate a named Nova KBM engagement (Software Asset Management programme). The banking vertical page is the entry point to their bank case studies in the region.

source_name: Bankart job postings (technology-stack tell)
why_relevant: Vacancy texts for payment-processing IT roles name concrete systems, standards and vendors the processor works with — an indirect but high-signal route to the technology inventory of the Slovenian card ecosystem.

source_name: Payten / Asseco SEE — payment technology (ATM, POS, processing) group site
why_relevant: Payten (Asseco SEE Group, Warsaw-listed) supplies ATM/POS software, terminals, eCommerce and processing across SEE including Slovenia; Asseco SEE has historically been the regional importer/integrator for Wincor Nixdorf ATMs. Group listing status also means Asseco SEE publishes segment revenue and contract disclosures — a rare quantified view of vendor share.

source_name: Euronet — ATM network operator in Slovenia
why_relevant: Self-described leading independent ATM-solutions player in Slovenia. As an independent deployer it both competes with and supplies banks (ATM outsourcing, branding), so its Slovenian pages indicate where banks have outsourced their ATM estate rather than buying hardware directly.

source_name: Diebold Nixdorf SEC filings & investor materials
why_relevant: ATM hardware/software supplier active in the Slovenian market (Wincor Nixdorf estate). US-listed filings occasionally name European contract wins and give segment/regional context that private Slovenian vendors never disclose.

source_name: CompanyWall.si / eBonitete.si — vendor financials and credit ratings
why_relevant: Gives revenue/headcount trajectories for private Slovenian IT vendors that publish nothing themselves (e.g. Comtrade d.o.o. 2025 revenue ~EUR 33.5m, net profit ~EUR 3.75m, 321 employees; Halcom 2024 revenue ~EUR 13.9m, +15.65% YoY). Revenue jumps are a proxy for large bank project wins.

source_name: Genis d.o.o. — e-Računi / document workflow vendor
why_relevant: Slovenian DMS/e-invoicing vendor whose product pages describe two-way integration with external providers and banks' invoice flows. Relevant to the back-office software layer sold into financial institutions; product pages sometimes name integration partners.

source_name: NIL (part of Conscia) — network/security integrator, Slovenia
why_relevant: Established Slovenian infrastructure/security systems integrator; banks are a core vertical for this class of supplier. Its Slovenian corporate/reference pages are a candidate pointer to bank infrastructure engagements.

source_name: Unistar LC / Actual I.T. group — IT supplier to Slovenian financial institutions
why_relevant: Unistar LC (owned by Actual I.T. d.d.) is a long-established Slovenian IT integrator; Actual I.T. is described as serving multiple Slovenian banks. LinkedIn company pages and posts are often where these vendors announce project wins, since their own sites carry little news.

source_name: TED (Tenders Electronic Daily) — Slovenian financial-IT notices
why_relevant: Systemic Slovenian commercial banks are private and outside procurement law, but state-linked financial entities (SID banka, SDH, Banka Slovenije, public funds) do publish banking-IT tenders. Award notices name the winning vendor and contract value — the only hard-priced datapoints available in this cell.

source_name: openprocurements.com (SI) — Slovenian public procurement aggregator
why_relevant: CPV-indexed browsing of Slovenian public tenders for computer-related services, where SRC, Unistar, Comtrade and similar vendors appear as suppliers. Useful for sizing these vendors' overall capability and confirming they are the same actors selling into banks, even though bank contracts themselves are absent.
